precepts.text: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the Sabbath day, that they might find an accusation against him.
precepts.point: And they watched him. Who is the they that watched him? The Pharisees. So they was always looking for accusations against Christ. Following him, following him, seeing is he going to slip up that we might accuse him. Remember what Christ said: if they do it unto you, surely they have done it unto me. They follow you block to block, state to state, camp corner to camp corner; surely they have done it unto Christ.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
Mark says “they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.” Who is the they that watched him? Luke names them: “And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.”

The scribes and Pharisees were always looking for accusations against Christ. Following him, following him, watching to see if he would slip up so they could accuse him.

Remember what Christ said: if they do it unto you, surely they have done it unto me. They follow us block to block, state to state, camp corner to camp corner, looking for something to accuse. Surely they did it unto Christ first.

precepts.text: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned. The judging Christ forbids is condemning someone. You cannot pronounce a person damned; judge not before the time, because you may be headed to the same place you are sending him.
precepts.point: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
“Judge not, that ye be not judged” is Christianity's favorite scripture, so go to Luke to see what it means: “Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned.” Luke explains Matthew. To judge here means to condemn someone. Judge not, condemn not: that is the precept of it.

So you cannot say someone is damned. You cannot say someone blasphemed the Holy Ghost. That ain't your call to make and that ain't your place. Vengeance and judgment belong to the Lord. “Judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come”, who will bring to light the hidden things of darkness; in that day we will all know who made it and who didn't, and who was doing right or only pretending to.

And look at the one making the call. I'm going to say he blasphemed the Holy Ghost, but I'm out here messing with these hoes, endorsing gang culture, going to the bars and getting drunk every other week, robbing women and robbing my congregation and spending their hard-earned money on my clothes and debauchery. But he's condemned? Get out of here, man. Judge not before the time, because your behind might go to the same place their behind is going.

That is Matthew 7 read with Luke 6: “For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged”; with what condemning you condemn, you'll be condemned too. You say your brother blasphemed while a beam is in your own eye and you are blaspheming more. Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye. We are all a work in progress, and the same mercy God had on David and Manasseh can be extended to you.

precepts.text: Why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? The man who hears and does is built on the rock and endures when the flood beats on the house. Brothers asking about deep prophecy while still on pornography need to learn themselves first.
precepts.point: In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.” What comes out of his mouth is what is in him.

“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” Why are you calling me Lord, Lord, and don’t do the things I tell you to do? “Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.” “But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell.”

The one built on Christ, which is the rock, is the one that is applying it. Applying it is the whole key. That is what strengthens the foundation and lets us endure when tribulations come. Wisdom teaches us that, and it is plain to understand. In that day men will say, Lord, Lord, did not I prophesy? Yes, but you still didn’t do what I told you to do. You were out on the street teaching, but you were a hypocrite; you weren’t living it.

Brothers sometimes come up wanting to understand the deep prophecies. Brother, let’s first help you get off of Pornhub. Why are you in Revelation trying to understand these archangels? You have to let that stuff go. You know prophecy, but you don’t know you yet. Learn you, so you are able to live it, and then instruct people wisely and teach them how to serve God.

precepts.text: Why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? You cannot just say you love the Lord, that you believe in the God of Israel, and do nothing of what he says: not loving your neighbour, holding grudges and envy, respecting leadership above your own husband who is Christ in the house.
precepts.point: All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him?

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” “the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” What the Lord weighs is actions: if it came out of your mouth, are you going to do it?

You cannot just say you love the Lord, that you believe in the God of Israel, and do nothing of what he says: not loving your neighbour, holding grudges and envy, respecting leadership above your own husband who is Christ in the house.

Saying, I have a personal relationship with God, God knows my heart, God loves me no matter what: that is arrogancy coming out of the mouth. The scripture says he loves you if you keep the commandments. Hannah said, “let not arrogancy come out of your mouth.”

precepts.text: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company; Saul separated David from his company for no reason, a mark of blessing on David.
precepts.point: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them; everybody knew he was the one really putting his life on the line and doing the work, even though he had no throne.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
“Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.”

“Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand.” He basically demoted the brother, putting his own armourbearer away from his presence for no reason. Saul separated David from his company, and that is a mark of blessing on David.

precepts.text: The same list names Simon called Peter and Judas the brother of James, showing the differing names for the same men.
precepts.point: Judas the brother of James is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude or Thaddaeus so as not to be associated with the traitor.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
Luke's own list shows the differing names for the same men: “Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alpheus, and Simon called Zelotes, And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.”

Where Matthew has Simon the Canaanite, Luke has “Simon called Zelotes”; where Matthew has Lebbeus Thaddeus, Luke has “Judas the brother of James.” And Luke keeps Judas the brother of James apart from “Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.” They are not the same man.
